package_info.why_malicious: These packages were created en masse to flood the npm ecosystem, causing denial of service, SEO poisoning, and serving as vectors for malware, referral scams, and crypto scams. The packages themselves are either empty or contain links to malicious websites, exploiting npm's reputation to boost malicious domains in search engines and disrupt the registry.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of published npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code exposes or redirects to a malicious website URL, enabling SEO poisoning and potential user redirection to malware or scam sites.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages do not simply export or link to unrelated external websites, especially those known for scams or malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages provide useful code or libraries, not just links to external, potentially harmful sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may link to documentation or homepages, but not in bulk or to known scam/malware domains.
key_indicators: Package content is only a URL or link to an external site
Domain is associated with scams, malware, or referral abuse

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package metadata advertises a malicious website as its homepage, increasing the site's SEO ranking and potentially luring users to visit it.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk creation of packages with homepages pointing to the same or similar malicious domains is a strong indicator of SEO poisoning or scam campaigns.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages have homepages related to the project, not unrelated scam or malware sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may link to their own documentation or project site.
key_indicators: Homepage field points to known scam/malware/referral domains
Pattern of mass package creation with similar metadata

attack_chain.action: Threat actor creates and publishes a large number of empty or near-empty npm packages with links to malicious or scam websites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Floods the npm registry, causing service instability and SEO poisoning.

attack_chain.action: Users or automated systems encounter these packages, potentially visiting the linked malicious sites or being exposed to malware/scam content.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware infection, referral scam participation, or exposure to crypto scams.

attack_chain.action: The volume of package publishing and access causes Denial of Service (DoS) on the npm registry, resulting in 'Service Unavailable' errors.
attack_chain.leads_to: Disruption of npm services and ecosystem trust.

behavioral_signatures: Bulk publishing of packages with minimal or no code
Packages exporting or linking only to external URLs
Homepage/repository fields pointing to known scam or malware domains
file_indicators: index.js or main file containing only a URL or export statement
package.json with homepage/repository fields set to suspicious domains
network_indicators: High volume of requests to npm registry from single or coordinated sources
Domains/IPs associated with known scam, malware, or referral campaigns
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mass publication of packages with minimal content and external links, especially those pointing to known malicious or scam domains. Flag packages with homepage or repository fields matching threat intelligence IOCs. Detect unusual spikes in package publishing or access patterns that could indicate a DoS or SEO poisoning campaign.
